title: Western Diocesan Uses (Iberian, French, German) and Religious-Order Liturgical Depth

traditions.label: Zaragoza Diocesan Use (Missale Caesaraugustanum)
traditions.family: Western diocesan use (Iberian / Crown of Aragon)
traditions.scope: Printed diocesan Mass-book witnesses attributed to the Archdiocese of Zaragoza (1485–1598), excluding monastic or Hospitaller house missals such as Sigena.
traditions.coverage_note: Documents the 1485 Paulus Hurus editio princeps (via inspected sheet-reuse scholarship) and the 1522–1598 inspected Usuarium census, with 1498 as a provisional incunable lead; medieval manuscripts, body-text collations, and post-1570 reception remain open.

traditions.label: València Diocesan Use (Missale Valentinum)
traditions.family: Western diocesan use (Iberian / Crown of Aragon)
traditions.scope: Printed diocesan Mass-book witnesses attributed to the See of València (1492–1528).
traditions.coverage_note: Documents the inspected 1509 and 1528 Usuarium printed witnesses and records the 1492 Venice Hamman incunable as a provisional lead; medieval manuscripts, body collation, and Tridentine transition remain open.

traditions.label: Tarragona Metropolitan Use (Missale Tarraconense)
traditions.family: Western diocesan use (Iberian / Crown of Aragon)
traditions.scope: Printed metropolitan Mass-book witnesses attributed to the Archdiocese of Tarragona (1499–1550).
traditions.coverage_note: Documents the inspected 1550 Lyon Septgranges printing (two catalogued copies) and records the 1499 Rosenbach Tarragona incunable as a provisional lead; earlier manuscripts and post-1570 reception remain open.

traditions.label: La Seu d'Urgell Diocesan Use (Missale Urgellense)
traditions.scope: Printed diocesan Mass-book witnesses attributed to the Diocese of Urgell (1536–1557).
traditions.coverage_note: Documents the inspected 1536 Zaragoza Coci and 1557 Lyon Septgranges-widow witnesses; earlier reported 1509 Venice printings, medieval manuscripts, and post-1570 transition remain open.

traditions.label: Toulouse Metropolitan Use (Missale Tolosanum)
traditions.scope: Printed Mass-book witnesses attributed to the Metropolitan See of Saint-Étienne of Toulouse (1501–1832).
traditions.coverage_note: Documents the inspected Usuarium census spanning pre-Tridentine prints (1501–1552), late-18th-century Neo-Gallican era prints (1773–1774), and Restoration-era printing (1832); original page inspection, Brienne reform collation, and 19th-century Romanization remain open.

traditions.label: Tours Metropolitan Use (Missale Turonense)
traditions.scope: Printed Mass-book witnesses attributed to the Metropolitan Cathedral of Tours (1485–1784), while keeping the collegiate basilica of Saint-Martin de Tours (1529) explicitly bounded.
traditions.coverage_note: Documents the inspected Usuarium census (1485, 1493, 1517, 1529 St-Martin, 1533, 1784); original imprint collation, cathedral-vs-St-Martin divergence, Conzié Neo-Gallican revisions, and 19th-century Romanization remain open.

traditions.label: Verdun Diocesan Use (Missale Virdunense)
traditions.scope: Printed diocesan Mass-book witnesses attributed to the Diocese of Verdun (1509–1829).
traditions.coverage_note: Documents the inspected Usuarium census across 1509, 1554, 1699, 1779, and 1829; original page inspection, episcopal reform acts (Psaulme, Desnos), and textual comparison remain open.

traditions.label: Meaux Diocesan Use (Missale Meldense)
traditions.scope: Printed diocesan Mass-book witnesses attributed to the Diocese of Meaux (1556–1845).
traditions.coverage_note: Documents the inspected Usuarium census (1556, 1836, 1845) and explicitly registers the landmark 1709 Neo-Gallican Missale Meldense (Ballard / Bissy / Ledieu controversy) as a high-priority acquisition gap pending direct Gallica page verification.

traditions.label: Bordeaux Metropolitan Use (Missale Burdegalense)
traditions.scope: Printed metropolitan Mass-book witness attributed to Saint-André Cathedral of Bordeaux (1543).
traditions.coverage_note: Documents the inspected 1543 Paul Berton printing (Usuarium 5812 / Amiet 210); earlier medieval manuscripts, later Tridentine/Neo-Gallican editions, and textual collation remain open.

traditions.label: Grenoble Diocesan Use (Missale Gratianopolitanum)
traditions.scope: Printed diocesan Mass-book witness attributed to the Diocese of Grenoble (1497).
traditions.coverage_note: Documents the inspected 1497 incunable (Usuarium 7150 / Amiet 0413, BM Grenoble U.1119 Rés.); earlier manuscripts, 16th–18th-century prints, and possible regional intersections with Carthusian/Dauphiné liturgy remain open.

traditions.label: Halberstadt Diocesan Use (Missale Halberstatense)
traditions.scope: Printed diocesan Mass-book witness attributed to the Diocese of Halberstadt (c. 1498).
traditions.coverage_note: Documents the inspected Usuarium 5818 witness (BSB 2 Inc.s.a. 879 f, GW M24400 / bsb00032887); direct scan inspection, earlier manuscripts, and 16th-century Reformation closure remain open.

traditions.label: Lübeck Diocesan Use (Missale Lubicense)
traditions.scope: Printed diocesan Mass-book witnesses attributed to the Diocese of Lübeck (1486–c. 1505).
traditions.coverage_note: Documents the inspected c. 1505 Usuarium 7238 witness and records the 1486 Matthäus Brandis incunable (Usuarium 41 / ISTC im00659300) as a provisional lead; USTC 741258/676212 reconciliation and Reformation closure remain open.

traditions.label: Merseburg Diocesan Use (Missale Merseburgense)
traditions.scope: Printed diocesan Mass-book witness attributed to the Diocese of Merseburg (1502).
traditions.coverage_note: Documents the inspected 1502 Usuarium 7271 witness (UB Leipzig III/243, Amiet 591); direct imprint/body inspection and Reformation-era cessation remain open.

traditions.label: Benedictine Monastic Missals (Missale Benedictinum / Casinense / Romano-Monasticum)
traditions.scope: Selected non-Bursfelde, non-Cluniac Benedictine printed missal states (1481 generic Benedictine incunable, 1580 Cassinese Congregation missal, 1937 Missale Romano-Monasticum rubric extract); kept distinct from individual abbey uses, Bursfelde, and Cluny.
traditions.coverage_note: Documents three bounded printed/preliminary states without asserting a single unified Benedictine recension across independent congregations.
